Let me know if you encounter any problems.

Best,

Vincent

messages.body_plain:
Dear Hananeh,

I see I have not replied to your question from October. Probably because you were going to take part in the training and I assumed we would discuss your questions then. Also you hinted at a collaboration but then it went silent.

> My first question is: should I first resample the temperature data then merge acc data and temp ?

Yes, GGIR assumes that temperature is a column next to acceleration signals all with same resolution.

> My second question is: Should I put one csv file for 7 days of data collection for datadir?

No, you can put multiple data files in datadir.

> I get this error:
> Error in read.myacc.csv("C:../Pilot/M_d2.csv") : Timezone not specified, please provide at least desiredtz and consider specifying configtz.

I hope that after having followed the GGIR training the error is now easier to understand. You will need to specify argument desiredtz and possibly configtz if the experiments took place in a different time zone then where the accelerometers were configured.

Best, Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: MVPA
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

There are several reasons why MVPA in part 2 and part 5 may differ, here some of them:

- Part 2 uses the threshold defined with "mvpathreshold", while part 5 uses "threshold.mod" to derive MVPA, double check that the definition of these 2 parameters are coherent in your function call.
- Make sure you are comparing MVPA derived with similar bout duration ("mvpadur" in part 2, "boutdur.mod" in part 5).
- Estimates in part 2 are calculated over calendar days, in part 5 you have the option to look at MM (days defined from midnight to midnight), WW (waking up to waking up), or OO (sleep onset to sleep onset). Different definitions of days may lead to differences in the estimations.
- In part 2, any acceleration surpassing the MVPA threshold is classified as MVPA, in part 5, if the acceleration occurs during the sleep period time, then it would not be part of the MVPA as physical activity is a behaviour that occurs during the awake time.
- Some other small differences like to order in which the bouts are extracted and the days separated may also produce minor differences, but I would say that, if differences are large, are very likely because of any of the previous points.

Hope this helps.

Best,
Jairo

Here an example: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#:~:text=The%20bare%20minimum%20input%20needed%20for%20GGIR%20is%3A

Best,
Jairo

Thanks! I found a minor bug in GGIR that triggered the error that you were experiencing. You can try to install the branch issue1032_bugDuplicatesCalibration  <https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/tree/issue1032_bugDuplicatesCalibration>in which I tried to give a solution to your issue:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "issue1032_bugDuplicatesCalibration")

However, this might not be enough, note that the accelerations in your csv file do not seem to be in g units, but you are specifying that rmc.acc.unit = "g". The values in your csv seem very high to be g units, make sure what unit of measurement the empatica has, I am not sure of that.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: Error in part 1: "Cannot open the connection"
messages.subject_clean: Error in part 1: "Cannot open the connection"
messages.body_plain:
Dear Jairo

Thank you for your quick response!

To be honest, someone else wrote a script for me, since we wanted to integrate several things into the script that (I think) could not be done or were more difficult to do with GGIR (e.g. we worked with an algorithm that determines types of activities, and did not use cut points for determining levels of physical activity), which made it more complex to write the script (at least for me). So, I'm not 100% sure why g.part1 was run isolated, but based on the comments in the script, I think that's how we wanted to calibrate the data, and determine ENMO and nonwear. The remainder of the script is less based on GGIR, I believe.

However, after changing the code so that it starts from the GGIR function instead of the gpart.1 function (see below, changes marked in yellow), the code seems to run and the appropriate output appears in the right folder.

GGIR(mode = 1, datadir = folder_raw, outputdir = folder_ggi, f1 = length(dir(folder_raw)),

chunksize = 1, windowsizes = c(1, 900, 3600),
overwrite = FALSE, desiredtz = 'Europe/Brussels')

So, thank you very much for your help!

Kind regards

Veerle Van Oeckel

Hi,

messages.body_plain:
Hi Yue,

The file you are trying to use does not contain the raw accelerometer data in csv format, but the counts per epoch already processed in ActiLife. Not sure if that is what you want to use. In the GGIR function documentation, you have an example function call for externally derived ActiGraph count data, I copy/paste the information here, note you would need to adjust some parameters depending on your files and the methods you would like to use:

# For externally derived ActiGraph count data in .CSV format assuming
# a study protocol where sensor was not worn during the night:
GGIR(datadir = "/examplefiles",
           outputdir = "",
           dataFormat = "actigraph_csv",
           mode = 1:5,
           do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
           windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
           threshold.in <http://threshold.in> = round(100 * (5/60), digits = 2),
           threshold.mod = round(2500 * (5/60), digits = 2),
           threshold.vig = round(10000 * (5/60), digits = 2),
           extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",
           do.neishabouricounts = TRUE,
           acc.metric = "NeishabouriCount_x",
           HASPT.algo = "NotWorn",
           HASIB.algo = "NotWorn",
           do.visual = TRUE,
           includedaycrit = 10,
           includenightcrit = 10,
           visualreport = FALSE,
           outliers.only = FALSE,
           save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE,
           ignorenonwear = FALSE,
           HASPT.ignore.invalid = FALSE,
           save_ms5raw_without_invalid = FALSE)

Best,
Jairo

I encountered something weird while processing my accelerometer files. I use timewindow = c('MM') and data_masking_strategy = 2. I also use study_dates_file. No sleeplog (I attached the config file).

messages.subject: Re: GGIR/Part2_summary error/Epoch size
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jaslie,

"part5_agg2_60seconds" does only affect part 5 reports, and you are looking at part 2 reports. If you want to use an epoch of 60 seconds in part 2, then you would need to set "windowsizes = c(60, 900, 3600)". Please see the documentation for "windowsizes". In most cases, I would say you do not need an epoch of 60 seconds in part 2, note that by default you get MVPA estimated with different configurations in part 2, being one of them 60-second epochs. And, an epoch of 5 seconds is the setting I would recommend for the sleep-related calculations in parts 3 and 4.

Best,
Jairo

messages.subject: Re: GGIR/Part2_summary error/Epoch size
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Note that, even if you are using 5 seconds as the first number in windowsizes, in part 2 reports you get the column(s) [...]MVPA_E1M_[...], which contains MVPA calculated over 1-minute epochs (in the case this is the activity variable you are interested in from part 2). This makes this strategy compatible with continueing the sleep analysis with 5-second epochs as recommended, and then get all the activity variables in part 5 with 1-minute epochs by using "part5_agg2_60seconds = TRUE".

Best,
Jairo

messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I have issues processing accelerometer data for a participant using the Day Segment Analysis <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/TutorialDaySegmentAnalyses.html> approach in GGIR (v3.0-5).

The data was collected using GENEActiv wrist-worn accelerometers (100Hz) under natural conditions, where participants recorded their location and corresponding time per day. The purpose of using the Day Segment Analysis approach was to include only days of interest. This is the shell code:

GGIR(

  #======================
  #GENERAL PARAMS
  #======================
  mode = mode,
  datadir = datadir,
  outputdir = outputdir,
  f0 = f0,
  f1 = f1,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  do.imp = TRUE,
  idloc = 2,
  print.filename = TRUE,
  storefolderstructure = FALSE,
  #======================
  # PART 1
  #======================
  windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.anglex = TRUE,
  chunksize = 0.5,
  printsummary = TRUE,
  #=====================
  #PART 2
  #=====================
  data_masking_strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,
  hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 0,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  M5L5res = 10,
  winhr = 5,
  qlevels = NULL,
  qwindow = qwindow, #file directory to the activity diary in .csv format
  qwindow_dateformat = qwindow_dateformat,
  desiredtz = "Australia/Brisbane",
  ilevels = NULL,
  mvpathreshold = 100.6,
  #=====================
  #PART 3
  #=====================
  timethreshold = 10,
  anglethreshold = 5,
  ignorenonwear = FALSE,
  #====================
  #PART 4
  #====================
  includenightcrit = 16,
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  loglocation = NULL,
  outliers.only = FALSE,
  criterror = 0,
  relyonguider = FALSE,
  do.visual = TRUE,
  #===================
  #PART 5
  #===================
  threshold.lig = 45.8,
  threshold.mod = 93.2,
  threshold.vig = 418.3,
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  boutcriter = 0.8,
  boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 0.9,
  boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8,
  boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(10,20,30),
  boutdur.lig = c(1, 5, 10),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(1, 5, 10),
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  #=====================
  #REPORT
  #=====================
  do.report=c(2,5),
  visualreport = TRUE,
  dofirstpage = TRUE,
  viewingwindow = 1
)

The code works because I successfully processed a different participant. The difference between the two are their activities. The participant that I have issues processing the accelerometer data, had additional days of recording that are not of interest, which I excluded in the activity log. An example of their activity log specified via the `qwindow()`function:

However, I receive the following error:

In the output folder, it does not contain any files relating to Part 5. In part2_daysummary.csv, there aren’t metrics computed in the file for the days of interest (highlighted in yellow below), but only the number of hours per segment:

 This is the quality plot:

If anyone can point out the issue or need more details please let me know!

Regards,

Kieu

> outputdir = "",
> dataFormat = "actigraph_csv",
> mode = 1:5,
> do.report = c(2, 4, 5),
> windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
> threshold.in <http://threshold.in> = round(100 * (5/60), digits = 2),
> threshold.mod = round(2500 * (5/60), digits = 2),
> threshold.vig = round(10000 * (5/60), digits = 2),
> extEpochData_timeformat = "%m/%d/%Y %H:%M:%S",
> do.neishabouricounts = TRUE,
> acc.metric = "NeishabouriCount_x",
> HASPT.algo = "NotWorn",
> HASIB.algo = "NotWorn",
> do.visual = TRUE,
> includedaycrit = 10,
> includenightcrit = 10,
> visualreport = FALSE,
> outliers.only = FALSE,
> save_ms5rawlevels = TRUE,
> ignorenonwear = FALSE,
> HASPT.ignore.invalid = FALSE,

>

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Computing cosinor metrics
messages.body_plain:
Hi Pedro,

For output variable names starting with "cosinor" these are all calculated based on the time series without invalid epochs, meaning: set to NA. As a result, GGIR uses all available valid data in the recording to fit the model and is not biased by period of non-wear time. In that way we avoid the need to require X number consecutive valid days. The only criteria you may want to set for yourself is the minimum number of days and the minimum amount of valid data in the recording as a whole.

In relation to IV and IS it may be good to emphasize that their implementation has never been properly evaluated as documented in the GGIR vignette. However, the code has  finally been evaluated and revised with external help and I hope to be able to include these updates in a next GGIR release.

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: class_name & class_id not very clear
messages.body_plain:
For reference, this is what one of my behavioralcodes CSV file looks like:

Here's my best guess on some of the components of the class names:
spt/day -> In the sleep period time window (spt) or not in the sleep period time window (day). spt_sleep is the estimated time asleep in the SPT-window; spt_wake_* classes are estimated time awake in the SPT-window.
IN/LIG/MOD/VIG/MVPA -> Levels of activity (Inactive, Light, Moderate, Vigorous, Moderate+Vigorous)
unbts/bts -> Unbouts and bouts. Unbouts are typically short(er) bursts of a given class. Bouts are sustained periods in given class.

messages.subject: Re: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.subject_clean: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.body_plain:
hi all, I came across this message to the forum about GGIR
mis-classifying large segments of what is most likely sleeping time as non-wear
time, and skewing sleep outputs.

We saw very similar findings when we ran GGIR with the
latest version, and saw that sleep periods were truncated and estimates of
sleep time to be reduced.

We tried re-running the data again with the parameter
“ignorenonwear = false” in Part 3, and the data look much better.

We will also try running it to keep using the older
approach by setting the  argument nonwear_approach to “2013” but haven’t
done this yet.

We are also looking into altering the window size parameter
of defining nonwear.

It seemed that Jairo in reply to earlier post suggested using
a 75 minute as opposed to 60 min window. We will try this as well but I am not
sure that will be a good solution, since we saw occurrences when very long
periods (> 75 min), large portions of the sleep period,  were flagged as
non-wear.

Have others run into this and if so, does anyone have any other suggestions or recommendations on how
to address this?

We are also interested in measures of waking physical
activity, sedentary behavior, and also the non-parametric daily activity (for
example, L5, M10, intradaily variability, interdaily stability) so not sure we
want to completely disregard what is considered non-wear outside of the sleep
period.
thanks all!

On Friday, December 1, 2023 at 9:08:55 AM UTC-5 Jairo Hidalgo Migueles wrote:
> Hi Pieter,
>
> Thank you for reporting this. May I ask if the actigraph device was initialized with the idle sleep mode turned on? That low variability in the acceleration for such a long time is very unlikely if the devices was being worn. You may also consider increasing the time for the longest windowsize, default is 1 hour (3600 seconds). It seems like some people may deep sleep until ~75 minutes, it is not frequent but still possible. Either way, I think this is quite a specific case which does now allow for evaluation of the nonwear algorithm.
>
> Best,
> Jairo
>
> El miércoles, 29 de noviembre de 2023 a las 16:59:25 UTC+1, Pieter-Jan Marent escribió:
> > Dear all
> >
> > After rerunning my dataset with the latest GGIR version (3.0-1), some default settings have been changed. Non-wear detection is now version 2023 which can have some important implications on sleep period detection. The default version of the non-wear window (argument windowsizes) is 1h (3600 seconds) and this long window is now flagged entirely as non-wear (in stead of the 15 min in 2013 version), see vignette or https://www.accelting.com/updates/ggir-release-3-0-0/. It seems like this can lead to potential errors in sleep period time detection. This is a warning/question to further investigate.
> >
> > To illustrate my concern with a real example of my dataset (wrist-worn actigraph):
> >
> > One of my participants indicated in their diary that they went to bed at 00.35 (time in bed) and fell asleep at 00.45 (sleep time). Time in bed was used in a sleep log to aid sleep period time detection.
> >
> > When using the 2013 version of non-wear detection (previously default), sleep onset was found to be at 0:42:00. Which is in line with the visual inspection of the raw data and the diary.
> >
> > When using the 2023 version of non-wear detection (default in version 3.0-1), sleep onset was found to be at  2:15:00. The reason for this 1,5h difference is that the 2023 version flagged the whole first hour of sleep as non-wear, where the 2013 only found a small portion to be non-wear. Since the argument "ignorenonwear" is set to TRUE (default), SPT detection only started after this non-wear hour. Resulting in this important misclassification.
> >
> > I have added screenshots from the visual report, but of course checked these findings in the csv files.
> >
> > And this is not the only case, I have another night where sleep efficiency scores dropped from 96% to 79% because of this change in non-wear classification.
> >
> > Could someone confirm this? How is it possible that during sleep, non-wear detection is triggered?
> >
> > Always happy to share my script and the files if needed, but this was more a general warning/question.
> >
> > Warm regards,
> > Pieter-Jan
> >
> > PS/ on a higher level: any non-wear in this night seems to be a mistake as the participant did not indicate taking it off the device + even if they removed it after falling asleep, you would suspect a clear "wake during the night" when they put the device back on which is not shown in the data...
> >
> >
> >

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error When Running GGIR Parts 1,2,3,4,5
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I was encountering this same error and think I figured out the issue. I was recently running a GGIR shell script  (GGIR version: 3.0.5) to process selected data files within a larger directory. To do so, I specified f0 = 14 and f1 = 16. However, each time I ran the script it crashed during the function g.report.part2. I debugged the error in R Studio and noticed a potential issue with the code and found a workaround I wanted to share.

The code above is a screenshot from g.report.part2. The following for loop iterates through i = 14, 15, 16 in my case. However, since the total number of files in the fnames vector is 3, attempting to access fnames[i] (which only contains 3 files) results in a null ending to the file path "fname2read". This causes the function to crash creating the error below.

As a workaround, I simply copied the files to a new directory and changed the path in "datadir" to point to this new directory. I then left f0 = 1 and removed f1 (since it defaults to the length of the directory).  This fixed my error and allowed me to run a subset of all my .gt3x files.

Hopefully this helps!

Sincerely,
Michael Melville

messages.body_plain:
Dear Jannick,

I am not able to reproduce your error with the file and script you sent.

Note that you have overwrite = FALSE, which could be the explanation as that will keep giving you the old results.

You are processing a file with no meaningful data, so we expect GGIR not to produce any output, especially not in part 4 and 5.

> Report part 4 loading all the milestone data from part 4 this can take a few minutes report not stored, because no results available

This is not an error, but just a notification that there are no results for part 4. It is then up to you to understand from the part 2 output that there is no meaningful data to use for part 4 and that that is why part 4 shows no results. As I am aware that this notification is confusing for some, I removed a few months ago. If you still get this message then that means GGIR was not successfully updated for you.

Best,
Vincent

messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: class_name & class_id not very clear
messages.body_plain:
Mike's explanation is correct. Part 5 variables are documented in the vignette and in the auto-generated part5 variable dictionary (added in autumn 2023).

I assumed that if a GGIR user is familiar with those variables you will be able to deduce what the class names are in the behaviouralcodes.csv. But, I can update the documentation to clarify this a bit more.

> However, I also think it might be useful for some of the users to maybe document somewhere the requirements for a given data point to be categorized into one of the categories like an acceleration threshold or something.

This is documented in inspecting the output in the vignette and in the documentation of the input parameters. Further, the way GGIR classifies intensity levels has been described in papers I was a co-author on, and it is discussed in our training course https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/ . Later this year we hope to write a dedicated vignette chapter to summarise all that...

> In my case I'd like to detect significant sleep disturbances during the night and I smoothed the datapoints over 1min and now came to the threshold in class_id of 1.2 leading to a "significant" sleep disturbance. However, it feels weird to kind of guess this threshold since I don't really know the thoughts behind these class_id's in the first place.

This is documented in the vignette, these are codes to refer to classes and averaging them makes no sense just like you wouldn't average participant ID numbers. Instead you should maybe use majority vote. Either way I do not understand why you are take that route, GGIR facilitates this for you with argument "part5_agg2_60seconds".

I am responding to the google group on a voluntary and unpaid basis. If you have more questions please consider our GGIR training course options: https://www.accelting.com/ggir-training/. Further, I'd be happy to offer personal consultancy session(s).

Kind regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

Grace

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Time change winter-summer
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nina,

No this is not done, because I did not see how we can do it meaningfully. If you know of any literature that has proposed a way to do this then let me know. I vaguely remember that there was a study by a Newcastle UK group that warned clinical trials not to test sleep during DST nights.

My concerns:
A person may keep their normal rhythm and wake up earlier/later, or go to bed earlier/later anticipating the clock change. It would then be dangerous to start adjust time accordingly.
The change in day length is unlikely to affect all behaviour equally. Possibly sleep and inactivity behaviours are more affected than active behaviours.

A possible solution could be that we add a GGIR parameter to instruct it to drop the two days surrounding DST? What do you think?

Note that column dur_day_spt_min in part 5 also tracks the window length.

Best wishes,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Question related to Output part 2
messages.body_plain:
Hi Hana,

I am not sure I understand your question. GGIR does not generate 7-day summaries.
Please be specific about the variable names you are comparing and any other detail about your data or analysis that could help us understand the issue.

For most GGIR reports recording level averages are provided as a plain average and as a weighted average. All of which should be reproducible from the day/night level values. GGIR directly used those day/night level reports to generate the recording (person) level summary.

Thanks,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

messages.body_plain:
Hello Michael,

Normally we would expect that for most of the 16 files process in part 1 there is also output available in part 2. Selecting files 14-16 is then problematic. In that case I would just use f0 = 1 and f1 = 0 which tells GGIR to process all available files.

On the other hand, I think f0=14 and f1=16 can be handled one additional line of code... Could you install the following test version of GGIR and let me know if this addresses your issue?

install.packages("remotes") # if you do not have remotes installed
remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref=  "issue1064_resetf0_part2report")

Thanks,

Vincent

messages.subject: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5
messages.subject_clean: Day Segment Analysis: Clarification with outputs for Part 2 and Part 5
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

Again, I really appreciate that there is this forum to ask questions about using GGIR to process accelerometer data.

Regarding activity-log based segmentation, my understanding is that it is implemented in Part 2 and Part 5 as outlined in the main GGIR vignette: 4 Implementation in GGIR <https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/TutorialDaySegmentAnalyses.html>. The exceptions are bouted and unbouted behaviour, which only provides a full-day summary, as noted in a previous thread discussion here <https://groups.google.com/g/rpackageggir/c/vfHzdq9fTnQ/m/RUAqaB1MAQAJ>.

However, when I use the activity-log to segment my data, I noticed that Part 2 segments  the results according to the activity-log. However, Part 5 outputs a full-day summary. Is this correct or am I missing something? In addition, Part 5 does not provide results for all the days recorded, even though Part 2 does.

For example, I have one participant with 5 days of recording that I am interested in and have ran the following GGIR code and using qwindow() to read the activity log:

GGIR(
  #======================
  #GENERAL
  #======================
  mode = mode,
  datadir = datadir,
  outputdir = outputdir,
  f0 = f0,
  f1 = f1,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  do.imp = TRUE,
  idloc = 2,
  print.filename = TRUE,
  storefolderstructure = FALSE,
  #======================
  # PART 1
  #======================
  windowsizes = c(5, 900, 3600),
  do.cal = TRUE,
  do.enmo = TRUE,
  do.anglex = TRUE,
  chunksize = 0.5,
  printsummary = TRUE,
  #=====================
  #PART 2
  #=====================
  data_masking_strategy = 1,
  hrs.del.start = 0,
  hrs.del.end = 0,
  maxdur = 0,
  includedaycrit = 16,
  M5L5res = 10,
  winhr = 5,
  qlevels = NULL,
  qwindow = qwindow,
  qwindow_dateformat = qwindow_dateformat # %d/%m/%Y,
  desiredtz = "Australia/Brisbane",
  ilevels = NULL,
  mvpathreshold = 100.6,
  #=====================
  #PART 3
  #=====================
  timethreshold = 10,
  anglethreshold = 5,
  ignorenonwear = FALSE,
  #====================
  #PART 4
  #====================
  includenightcrit = 16,
  def.noc.sleep = 1,
  loglocation = NULL,
  outliers.only = FALSE,
  criterror = 0,
  relyonguider = FALSE,
  do.visual = FALSE,
  #===================
  #PART 5
  #===================
  threshold.lig = 45.8,
  threshold.mod = 93.2,
  threshold.vig = 418.3,
  excludefirstlast = FALSE,
  boutcriter = 1,
  boutcriter.in <http://boutcriter.in> = 1,
  boutcriter.lig = 1,
  boutcriter.mvpa = 1,
  boutdur.in <http://boutdur.in> = c(5, 10, 30, 60),
  boutdur.lig = c(5, 10, 30, 60),
  boutdur.mvpa = c(5, 10, 30, 60),
  timewindow = c("WW"),
  #=====================
  #REPORT GENERATION
  #=====================
  do.report=c(2, 5),
  visualreport = TRUE,
  dofirstpage = TRUE,
  viewingwindow = 1
)

part2_daysummar.csv and part2_daysummary_longformat.csv provides results for the five days and segments. However, part5_daysummary only provides full day summaries with only three days of results and part5_personalsummary only one day of results.

What I was hoping to see in Part 5 was a summary of the minutes in different physical activity levels according to the segments, not full day summaries. Any clarification would be appreciated.

Attached are the .csv files for Part 2 (day summary), Part 5 (day and person) and the meta .Rdata file.

Regards,
Kieu

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] About physical activity intensity classification
messages.body_plain:
That depends on which MVPA estimate from the GGIR you are using and how you configured the related input parameters.

If you are using MVPA estimates based on bouts then MOD + VIG is not necessarily the same as MVPA in a bout, unless you do not allow for gaps in bouts and the minimum bout duration equals the epoch length.

Best,
Vincent

Thanks Nina,

I had a look at the data you sent and it seems this to me that this is an issue with the code used for the visualisation and not with the underlying analysis because the rest of the results and time series look fine to me.

It is known that the visual report is not always perfect and it is better not to use it as a basis for data quality assessment, as is clarified in the vignette: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/GGIR/vignettes/GGIR.html#231_Key_general_arguments

Rewriting and improving the code for the visual report would require a significant time investment. If anyone is interesting in doing this work or hiring me (and/or Jairo) to do it then please contact me.

Best wishes,

Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Re: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.subject_clean: [GGIR] Re: Question/Warning on new default non-wear detection and its implication on SPT detection
messages.body_plain:
Question to Jairo: do the updates in https://github.com/wadpac/GGIR/pull/1067 that I just merged in the new 3.0-7 release offer a better solution or guidance in relation to this?
I suspect those updates which entail the option to set HASPT.ignore.invalid = NA, is mainly relevant to studies who know that the accelerometer is not worn during the night, while here the issue is that the accelerometer is expected to be throughout the night. Nonetheless, maybe it does help...

Note: 3.0-7 is only available on GitHub, install with remotes::install_github("wadpac/GGIR", ref = "3.0-7").

Question to Ari and Pieter-Jan: Which accelerometer brand are you using? I am wondering whether this is issue could be specific to certain accelerometer brand(s). For example, I imagine that ActiGraph with idle sleep mode turned on might become idle when a person somehow does not move for more than an hour.

Kind regards,
Vincent

On Friday, 16 February 2024 at 4:38 PM, Ari Shechter <ari.sh...@gmail.com> wrote:

> hi all, I came across this message to the forum about GGIR mis-classifying large segments of what is most likely sleeping time as non-wear time, and skewing sleep outputs.
>
> We saw very similar findings when we ran GGIR with the latest version, and saw that sleep periods were truncated and estimates of sleep time to be reduced.
>
> We tried re-running the data again with the parameter “ignorenonwear = false” in Part 3, and the data look much better.
>
> We will also try running it to keep using the older approach by setting the argument nonwear_approach to “2013” but haven’t done this yet.
>
> We are also looking into altering the window size parameter of defining nonwear.
>
> It seemed that Jairo in reply to earlier post suggested using a 75 minute as opposed to 60 min window. We will try this as well but I am not sure that will be a good solution, since we saw occurrences when very long periods (> 75 min), large portions of the sleep period, were flagged as non-wear.
>
> Have others run into this and if so, does anyone have any other suggestions or recommendations on how to address this?
>
> We are also interested in measures of waking physical activity, sedentary behavior, and also the non-parametric daily activity (for example, L5, M10, intradaily variability, interdaily stability) so not sure we want to completely disregard what is considered non-wear outside of the sleep period.
> thanks all!
> On Friday, December 1, 2023 at 9:08:55 AM UTC-5 Jairo Hidalgo Migueles wrote:
> > Hi Pieter,
> >
> > Thank you for reporting this. May I ask if the actigraph device was initialized with the idle sleep mode turned on? That low variability in the acceleration for such a long time is very unlikely if the devices was being worn. You may also consider increasing the time for the longest windowsize, default is 1 hour (3600 seconds). It seems like some people may deep sleep until ~75 minutes, it is not frequent but still possible. Either way, I think this is quite a specific case which does now allow for evaluation of the nonwear algorithm.
> >
> > Best,
> > Jairo
> >
> > El miércoles, 29 de noviembre de 2023 a las 16:59:25 UTC+1, Pieter-Jan Marent escribió:
> > > Dear all
> > >
> > > After rerunning my dataset with the latest GGIR version (3.0-1), some default settings have been changed. Non-wear detection is now version 2023 which can have some important implications on sleep period detection. The default version of the non-wear window (argument windowsizes) is 1h (3600 seconds) and this long window is now flagged entirely as non-wear (in stead of the 15 min in 2013 version), see vignette or https://www.accelting.com/updates/ggir-release-3-0-0/. It seems like this can lead to potential errors in sleep period time detection. This is a warning/question to further investigate.
> > >
> > > To illustrate my concern with a real example of my dataset (wrist-worn actigraph):
> > >
> > > One of my participants indicated in their diary that they went to bed at 00.35 (time in bed) and fell asleep at 00.45 (sleep time). Time in bed was used in a sleep log to aid sleep period time detection.
> > >
> > > When using the 2013 version of non-wear detection (previously default), sleep onset was found to be at 0:42:00. Which is in line with the visual inspection of the raw data and the diary.
> > >
> > > When using the 2023 version of non-wear detection (default in version 3.0-1), sleep onset was found to be at 2:15:00. The reason for this 1,5h difference is that the 2023 version flagged the whole first hour of sleep as non-wear, where the 2013 only found a small portion to be non-wear. Since the argument "ignorenonwear" is set to TRUE (default), SPT detection only started after this non-wear hour. Resulting in this important misclassification.
> > >
> > > I have added screenshots from the visual report, but of course checked these findings in the csv files.
> > >
> > > And this is not the only case, I have another night where sleep efficiency scores dropped from 96% to 79% because of this change in non-wear classification.
> > >
> > > Could someone confirm this? How is it possible that during sleep, non-wear detection is triggered?
> > >
> > > Always happy to share my script and the files if needed, but this was more a general warning/question.
> > >
> > > Warm regards,
> > > Pieter-Jan
> > >
> > > PS/ on a higher level: any non-wear in this night seems to be a mistake as the participant did not indicate taking it off the device + even if they removed it after falling asleep, you would suspect a clear "wake during the night" when they put the device back on which is not shown in the data...
> > >
> > >
> > >

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GeneActiv Lux Output
messages.body_plain:
Misia,

The epoch-by-epoch output, which includes a lightpeak column with lux values, is located in /output_folder/meta/ms5.outraw

In that folder you'll find a "behavioralcodes" CSV file and then another folder (I think the name depends upon activity thresholds) that contains 1 epoch-by-epoch CSV per recording.

Importantly, I think you need to fix your ms5-related configuration options to use an underscore (e.g., save_ms5rawlevels) instead of a period (e.g., save.ms5rawlevels in your code snippet above).

Hope that helps!
